title: Motor abstraction training generalizes to the refinement of specific movement patterns
title_zh: 抽象训练推广到具体运动模式的精炼
abstract: The ability to abstract the invariant structure of an experience while discarding incidental details underlies generalization across virtually every domain of human cognition, from vision and language to concept learning. Yet whether the motor system generates such abstractions and whether they causally contribute to skilled performance remain open questions. Here we introduce a paradigm in which human participants learned novel movement patterns by precisely copying unfamiliar handwritten characters. To examine the role of motor abstractions in this form of learning, participants were trained on markedly rotated versions of the characters, which recruited substantially different lower-level movements while still maintaining the relevant abstract movement trajectory. Across 11 experiments, abstraction training drove robust performance improvements that were comparable to having repetitive practice on the canonical form of each character. Moreover, this effect was largely motoric in nature: it did not require a visual template, sustained trajectory feedback or mental imagery, and was sensitive to the sequential structure of the movement trajectory. These findings establish a causal role for abstractions in motor learning, revealing that the motor system probably deploys abstractions in the earliest stages of skill acquisition.
abstract_zh: 几乎每个人类认知领域，从视觉和语言到概念学习，其背后的原理都是在经验中抽象不变的结构并丢弃偶然细节，从而实现泛化。然而，运动系统是否生成此类抽象以及它们是否对熟练表现起因果作用，仍是未解之题。本研究引入了一个范式，人类参与者通过精确复制陌生的手写字符来学习新的运动模式。为了探究此类运动抽象在该类学习中的作用，参与者接受了显著旋转版本字符的训练，这些训练招募了实质不同的低级运动，但仍然保持相关的抽象运动轨迹。在11个实验中，抽象训练带来了显著的性能提升，其效果与反复练习每个字符的规范形式相当。此外，该效果主要具有运动性质：不需要视觉模板、持续的轨迹反馈或心理意象，且对运动轨迹的顺序结构敏感。这些发现确立了抽象在运动学习中的因果作用，揭示运动系统可能在技能习得的最早阶段部署抽象。
